title: Variant selection and staged upgrade framework for reranker fleets (cross-encoder, multilingual)
creator: Luca Thompson
description:
Goal: Define a reproducible, low-risk framework to select cross-encoder reranker variants (including compact and quantized variants) and perform staged upgrades across multilingual fleets while maintaining quality SLAs and latency SLOs. Scope includes evaluation datasets, gating/regression checks, rollout rings, performance budgeting, and rollback criteria. This ticket produces the playbook, evaluation harness updates, and required dashboarding and PR checklists for safe upgrades. Context: we've observed non-linear latency regressions when moving from teacher-consistent models to denser cross-encoders in specific languages; compact variants reduce cost but sometimes degrade relevance for long-tail locales. We need a standardized decision flow that balances quality, latency, and cost.

Key constraints and trade-offs:
- Quality vs latency: highest-quality cross-encoders are often larger; we aim to prefer variants that reduce tail latency (P95) without >1.5% absolute drop in relevance metrics.
- Quantization/INT8 benefits vs numeric stability: quantized candidates need extra regression checks for hallucination and precision loss on numeric-heavy queries.
- Serving cost: dedicated pools must respect reserved capacity budgets; upgrades that increase token compute must be flagged to finance.
- Multilingual coverage: must evaluate per-language performance, not just aggregate metrics, with special attention to low-data languages (pt-BR, id, vi, ar).

Deliverables:
- Playbook document with decision tree and required artifacts for each upgrade (linked below)
- Automated regression harness changes to include multilingual test sets and latency noise injection
- Dashboards and alerts for candidate canaries (P50, P95, token cost, error rate, quality deltas per language)
- CI gates and PR checklist for model onboarding into production serving
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published in Confluence and linked from model catalog
Regression harness runs end-to-end in CI and fails the PR if any language shows >1.5% absolute NDCG drop or >10% traffic latency regression at P95
Canary rollout automation template created (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) with automatic rollback triggers
Dashboard for rerank candidates displays per-language metrics and is wired to alerting
Cost impact estimate for a candidate is calculated and attached to the model onboarding PR
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Local evaluation — run candidate vs baseline on benchmark sets (dev/test) and produce per-language NDCG/MRR
Stage 1: Shadow traffic in production for 72h with sampling (no user-visible changes) to capture latency profile and error modes
Stage 2: Canary 1% traffic for 24h; automated checks: quality/regression, P95 latency, error rate
Stage 3: Canary 5% for 48h with extended multilingual sampling and finance cost check
Stage 4: Gradual ring expansion (25% -> 100%) with manual sign-off at 25% if all gates pass
Rollback: automatic rollback if any gate fails; manual rollback if subtle regressions observed via human review
regression_checks: Per-language NDCG@10 and MRR delta thresholds (default: no >1.5% absolute drop)
Embedding-similarity drift checks on anchor queries
Stress latency test under synthetic 2x peak qps to check tail behavior
Hallucination/noise spot checks using numeric and entity-rich prompts
Token-level output stability checks for structured-output rerank signals
metrics: Quality: NDCG@10, MRR, precision@1 per language
Latency: P50,P95,P99 token-generation latency per model variant
Cost: GPU-ms per 1k queries and estimated monthly spend delta
Reliability: 5xx rate, model timeouts, memory OOMs
Regression: percent of queries with rank-order changes beyond threshold
